data.turoyo: I naqqa d ḥzelan am məhaǧər, l ḥoṯi səmla hawxa iḏa, mi zəʕṯo. <...> Balla-wakil mədulle, mfakfakke ṣawʕoṯa w mawfaqqe i kiyyo w azzən.
data.translation: When we saw the refugees, my sister did her hand like this, out of fear. <...> By God as witness, they rushed, prised open the fingers, took out the gum and went away.

rationale: Second Preterit example; loosening fingers contrasts with the inherited bread-breaking example and keeps the owner in context. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: No round-1 job exists. The supplied entry uses stem I for mfakfakle/mfakfək; this convention is preserved rather than replacing it with Q.
The clause explicitly loosens the sister’s fingers before removing the gum. It exemplifies lösen/losmachen, not bread crumbling, and requires no new numbered sense or idiom.
Supply the plural ending in kleine Brotstücke
rationale: After kleine the plural noun is Brotstücke; kleine Brotstück has lost its final e.

summary: Capitalize the noun Bissen in the gloss
rationale: Bissen is the German noun coordinated with Stück Brot, the object of brocken. Its lowercase initial is a spelling error.

summary: Finger als zu lösende Körperteile erweitern den bestehenden Lösesinn; die Kiyyo-Entnahme begründet keine neue Bedeutung.
